answer: Agents can require every new identity to post a refundable bond before receiving jobs, while random peer challenges test its signed work against hidden cases. If an identity fails, the protocol burns its bond and pays the challenger. A Sybil attacker must lock capital for every invented agent and risks losing each deposit; splitting one budget across many identities also reduces each agent’s earning power. The meadow, river, and pulse of activity can serve as challenge labels, but the economic bond supplies the defense.
